fullText:
Pre-game, captain John McGinn promised Aston Villa fans they could still expect "as much as possible" this season despite the high-profile exits of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans.

A battling performance in Austria backed those words up as, even in this defeat by PSG, Villa scared the European champions for a second time in 18 months, following their 5-4 Champions League last-eight defeat in 2025.

No Ollie Watkins, Emi Martinez and Ezri Konsa - given more time off after the World Cup - which allowed teenager Brian Madjo to finally show what he can do after Villa won their appeal to register him, and 19-year-old midfielder George Hemmings also getting a start.

The positives were also evident despite the loss, with Boubacar Kamara also playing his first competitive match since a serious knee injury in January.

Villa should be stronger for the Premier League season opener at Brighton on 23 August, with the club due to be active in the final two weeks of the transfer window.

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri is poised to join this week, while they have not given up on their chase for Bayern Munich midfielder Joao Palhinha.

Ever the perfectionist, boss Emery will be frustrated by the loss - especially as it was his fourth defeat in the competition - but as Villa enter a new era there is a lot of cause for optimism.

title: Lampard believes Haji Wright ready for Premier League
description: After struggling to find the field during the World Cup, Wright is ready to lead Coventry into the Premiership.
fullText:
The 2026-27 Premier League season begins next week, and 20 teams enter with dreams renewed for the new year. For Coventry City, who earned promotion to the Premier League after winning the EFL Championship, it will be a chance to compete in the top flight for the first time since the 2000-01 season. And USMNT forward Haji Wright will be a big part of their offense this season.

Wright was one of the major factors behind Coventry's promotion last season, with 18 goals and 2 assists in 40 appearances for the Sky Blues across all competitions. However, he struggled to find any playing time for the USMNT during the 2026 World Cup, with just two minute-long appearances logged for the tournament.

Still, Coventry has relied on him to score goals, and he's done that since he arrived there in August 2023. In 124 total appearances, he's scored 49 goals and added 11 assists. It's that kind of production that head coach Frank Lampard feels has prepared Haji Wright for the rigors of the Premier League.

"When you come into a job, you evaluate the talent in the squad and the need for goals at the top end of the pitch. Haji already had a record as such," Lampard said, speaking exclusively to Stars & Stripes FC. "He was playing on the left wing sometimes under the previous manager, but I felt quite quickly that he's a No. 9 and he prefers to be in that position too. I think it makes the most of his talents and attributes, with his speed, size and ability to run in behind defenses. It will be a big test for him, as with all the players, because there's a big gap with the Premier League. They must be focused on bridging that gap with belief. I think Haji absolutely has the talent to succeed here in the Premier League."

For Lampard, the hope is that Wright is able to continue his goal production to help keep Coventry in the top flight. Most teams that are promoted to the Premier League struggle in that first season, with a big percentage of them getting relegated back to the Championship after one year. Coventry hope to dodge the relegation slide and do what they can to stay afloat. And for Wright, it's a chance to show that he is a dependable striker in one of the best leagues in the world and that he can produce against some of the best defenses on the planet.

Coventry have a tall task ahead of them, as they open up the season on the road on August 21st to defending Premier League champions Arsenal. Three of their first four matches will come against teams that finished in the top 8 in last season's table: Arsenal, Manchester City, and Brighton & Hove Albion. It will truly be a big test for Haji Wright and the Sky Blues as they prepare for their first Premier League season in 25 years.

title: Doku 'not against' journalist who criticised him at World Cup
description: Jeremy Doku says he is "not against" the journalist who criticised his plan to leave the Belgium camp during the World Cup to attend the birth of his first child.
fullText:
Jeremy Doku says he is "not against" the journalist who criticised his plan to leave the Belgium camp during the World Cup to attend the birth of his first child.

Doku's wife Shireen was due to give birth during the second week of July and he told Reuters, external before the start of the tournament he intended to leave the camp to be at the birth even if his side were still in contention.

But it brought fierce criticism from L'Equipe channel presenter France Pierron, who labelled a father "completely useless" at the time of their child's birth.

L'Equipe later apologised and said Pierron's comments were "very far removed" from its values. The presenter also apologised but was taken off air until the end of the season of her show.

Doku eventually missed Belgium's 0-0 draw against Iran in the group stage to fly back to the UK for the birth of his son, Praise.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, external, Doku said he understood why some people questioned the timing of events.

"There was a lot of noise of course," the Manchester City winger said.

"I can understand why people felt like maybe this was orchestrated because it was too perfect.

"I also saw the journalist speak about me and the situation and all the people getting at her. But I just wanted to use this video as well to really... pray over her.

"I don't want to come at her in a way that most people did. I don't want people to be too harsh on her. We don't know what she has experienced. It's her opinion.

"She got fired and all these things. I never want this for a person. I'm not against her. I'm not angry at her or anything. She just said her opinion."

Doku played 86 minutes of Belgium's opening 1-1 draw with Egypt in Group G of the World Cup before missing their next game, with his absence explained as illness.

A Belgium statement later said, external that the 24-year-old travelled to London to be with his wife "with the approval of and accompanied by one of our team doctors".

title: Women's football shouldn't be penalised by Uefa boycott - Nandy
description: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy says women's footballers should not be "penalised" by a potential boycott of next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup.
fullText:
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy says women's footballers should not be "penalised" by a potential boycott of next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup, as hosts Poland say they have received no notice of any withdrawals from European teams.

European governing body Uefa and its 55 members have threatened to boycott Fifa competitions over its president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

Poland are due to host the tournament from 5-27 September, but are not the only Uefa nation involved - with England, Italy, Spain, Portugal and France all due to take part.

The Polish Football Association (PZPN) told BBC Sport on Tuesday that it had so far "not received any information regarding the possible withdrawal of any participating team from the tournament".

It added: "We believe that the current situation will be resolved swiftly, allowing young players from across the world to compete in Poland.

"Our priority remains to ensure the best possible conditions for the competition and for all participating teams. For many of these young players, this tournament represents an important milestone in their sporting careers, and we remain fully focused on delivering an event worthy of their talent and commitment."

Last week, the French Football Federation (FFF) said it intended to compete at the U20 World Cup while the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) also told BBC Sport that "so far, the Under-20 team is complying with the planned programme", including a friendly fixture against England later this week.

England's Football Association has not confirmed whether it will field a team for the World Cup. However, as things stand, coach Lydia Bedford's Young Lionesses squad are continuing preparations for the tournament.

The map showing world's division over Infantino

Trump says it would be 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino

Nandy told the BBC that she wants to see Infantino resign over his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, under which stakes in the World Cup and other competitions would be sold to private investors.

"We support the [English] FA in saying that football belongs to its fans, enough is enough, and it is time for a change at Fifa," Nandy said.

"I think [Infantino] should go, the time is up."

But she added she would not support a boycott of the U20 World Cup.

"I am not generally in favour of sporting boycotts full stop, because I think they divide people from one another, I think they unfairly penalise athletes and competitors who are not responsible for the reason that these boycotts take place," she said.

"What I would like to see actually is football coming together, resolving this, a change of leadership, a change of direction and a very clear message that football belongs to its fans and it will not have women and girls penalised when the women's game is going from strength to strength. And our Lionesses are leading the world in that."

title: Trump says would be 'terrible mistake' to oust embattled Infantino

fullText:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday it would be "a terrible mistake" to replace Gianni Infantino, the embattled FIFA president who tried, and failed, to sell off part of the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino came under renewed fire in an open letter signed by three confederations -- Europe's UEFA, North and Central America's CONCACAF and Asia's AFC -- accusing the world football boss of breaking trust "through deception".

But Trump backed Infantino, who awarded the US president a "FIFA Peace Prize" at the World Cup draw ceremony last year.

"FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino," Trump posted on Truth Social.

Trump called Infantino "fantastic" and said he "presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented".

"If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!" added Trump, who attended the World Cup final with Infantino last month.

Trump's backing of Infantino is at odds with US Soccer, who joined the voices lining up against the FIFA president.

Infantino launched, and then withdrew in the face of scathing criticism, a plan to bring private investment into FIFA competitions, including World Cups.

FIFA hit back on Saturday at efforts "to undermine" football's governing body and Infantino.

However, Monday's joint letter from UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC retorted: "Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding -- or demanding -- power to be held.

"When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned."

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is viewed as a potential challenger to Infantino, who will be up for re-election for a fourth and final term at the FIFA Congress in March, 2027. Candidates have to be declared by November 18.

Infantino had looked certain to be unopposed for a fourth term after overseeing a successful World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada until his plans were revealed.

The 56-year-old Swiss, who has been in situ for 10 years, has received the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) while South American governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive.

Individual member associations, not confederations, vote in the FIFA election,

Infantino has received support from CONCACAF's Mexico and two AFC members -- Kuwait and 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar, where he has a house.

UEFA's threat to boycott World Cups if the private investment plan went ahead proved pivotal in Infantino withdrawing his sell-off plan.

UEFA had called it "a shabby, opaque, backroom deal" and lashed out at Infantino again on Monday for a "failure of judgment".

After the furore, Infantino received "full support" of senior FIFA directors in an emergency meeting in Morocco last week, but the three confederations said that was meaningless.

The recent meeting, where "a select number of members of the FIFA Management Committee" were present, they said, "represents a continuation of the very pattern of conduct that brought us to this moment".

"It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him."

Infantino had been basking in the afterglow of the largest ever World Cup involving 48 teams until his plans divided the sport.

"The growth over the past decade has been real. But that progress was never the work of one individual," declared the letter.

"It was the product of FIFA, the Confederations, the Member Associations, and the thousands of people who dedicate their lives to the game.

"The expanded tournaments... were shared achievements, agreed together, delivered together."

Under Infantino's leadership "there is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness", they said.

"That is why we have taken this stance: not lightly and not alone, but together, and out of duty to the game we serve.

"Football's strength has always been its unity."

title: Parkinson withdraws from England Under-20 camp

title: Scotland and Dutch boards criticise ICC for World Cup changes
description: The cricket boards of Scotland and the Netherlands criticise the International Cricket Council for structural changes made to men's 50-over World Cup.
fullText:
The cricket boards of Scotland and the Netherlands have criticised the International Cricket Council for structural changes made to the men's 50-over World Cup.

Last month the ICC announced the main part of the tournament for 2027 would be 12 teams in two groups of six, rather than 14 as originally planned.

The three lowest-ranked qualifiers will instead be placed in a preliminary three-team Super Series, from which only the winner will progress.

It effectively means the likes of Scotland and the Netherlands face three qualifying tournaments to reach the main group stage of the World Cup.

A joint statement from Cricket Scotland and Royal Dutch Association (KNCB) said they had "significant concerns" about the "impact of these changes" along with the "process through which they have been introduced".

"The changes risk weakening the integrity and credibility of international cricket, and only highlights the importance of strong governance, transparent decision-making and effective engagement with members," the statement said.

"Changing those structures at short notice creates significant uncertainty, disrupts planning, and places additional operational and financial pressure on organisations that are already operating with limited resources."

BBC Sport has approached the ICC for comment.

ICC considers World Cup cuts & WTC semis in overhaul

Scotland scrape past UAE with one wicket & ball left

The changes to the World Cup were agreed during meetings at the ICC's annual conference held in Edinburgh in June.

However, BBC Sport understands nearly all associate members were kept in the dark over the changes despite being present at the conference.

Cricket Scotland and the KNCB said they remain "fully committed" to "working constructively with the ICC".

But the two boards accused the global governing body of being "disrespectful" in how they have handled some of the discussions following the announcement.

"Cricket Scotland, KNCB and other associate members met twice with the ICC, seeking official written communication on the changes and greater clarity around the processes involved," the statement added.

"We also requested positive action to strengthen future operational decision-making and an invitation to bilateral planning meetings with full members.

"Since the second meeting more than two weeks ago, there has been no further response from the ICC, which is disappointing and disrespectful given the significance of the issues raised."

The joint statement follows concerns raised by the World Cricketers' Association last month over the decision.

Scotland and the Netherlands are the two highest ranked associate members.

Their decision to issue such a pointed statement reflects frustrations outside of full members with aspects of ICC decision making.

BBC Sport understands proposals were tabled at the 2025 ICC annual conference to create a single-class of membership, rather than having associate and full members, but it did progress.

The statement added that the changes to the World Cup qualifying were a "setback" for associate members and "risk undermining the progress made in recent years to grow the global game".

"At a time when cricket is seeking to expand its reach, attract new audiences and strengthen its position on the international sporting landscape, reducing meaningful opportunities for emerging nations sends entirely the wrong message," it said.

The statement also called on the ICC to "re-engage with associate members" and to do so "openly" to enable the sport to develop outside of full members.

"Leaders in cricket have consistently spoken about their ambition for the sport to become truly global," added the statement.

"Providing meaningful opportunities for emerging nations to qualify for, and compete at, major events is fundamental to achieving that ambition.

"Decisions that reduce or limit those opportunities slow the progress being made to expand the game's reach and appeal and runs counter to those ambitions."

title: African quartet secure Women's World Cup places
description: Algeria, Morocco, Cameroon and Malawi all qualify for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil by reaching the semi-finals of the Women's Africa Cup of Nations.
fullText:
Algeria, Morocco, Cameroon and Malawi have all qualified for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil.

The Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) in Morocco is also acting as a qualifying tournament for next summer's tournament, with any country that makes the semi-finals earning their places at the World Cup.

Algeria beat 10-player Ivory Coast 2-1, with goals from Ines Khiri and Amira Ould Braham - after N'Sira Oudraogo was sent off when the Ivorians were 1-0 ahead - to reach the Wafcon last four and qualify for a Women's World Cup for the first time.

Goals from Sakina Ouzraoui Diki and Hanane Ait El Haj helped Morocco defeat South Africa 2-1 to claim their place, with Cameroon securing a 1-0 victory over Nigeria thanks to a spectacular 30-yard free-kick from 19-year-old Myriam Nyadjou.

The fourth spot was taken by Malawi, 153rd in the world rankings, who caused a huge shock by beating Ghana 2-1, coming from behind with goals from Temwa Chawinga and Rose Kadzere.

The Wafcon semi-finals will take place on Wednesday with Morocco taking on Cameroon before Algeria meet Malawi.

The four nations that lost in the Wafcon quarter-finals - Ghana, Ivory Coast, Nigeria and South Africa - still have a chance to qualify for the World Cup.

On Thursday, Ivory Coast play Ghana and Nigeria will face South Africa with the two winners going into the 10-nation intercontinental play-offs in November and December.

Out of those 10 countries in the play-offs, three will qualify for next summer's World Cup, which begins on 24 June and ends on 25 July.

England, Republic of Ireland, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland all still have a chance of qualifying from the European play-offs, which will take place from October to December.

Each of those five sides would need to win two two-legged ties to qualify.

There will be 32 nations competing at the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil and 18 of the qualifiers are now known.

Asia - Australia, China, Japan, North Korea, Philippines, South Korea.

title: Barcelona growing increasingly optimistic about signing World Cup winner

fullText:
Barcelona are currently involved in two of the most talked about transfer sagas in European football right now in Rodri and Julian Alvarez.

Rodri, in particular, has generated a lot of buzz in recent days after the midfielder chose to join Barcelona ahead of a move to Real Madrid.

Barcelona, though, must reach an agreement with Manchester City if they are to get their hands on the Spanish World Cup winner.

Rodri is keen on joining Barcelona. (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

According to Diario SPORT, there is total optimism within Barcelona regarding their chances of signing Rodri, with the club now treating the midfielder as their absolute priority.

The Catalans have already presented an improved offer to Manchester City, having realised their initial proposal of €45 million plus €5 million in variables fell well short of the English club's demands.

The report cites sources within the club insist they are on the right track, with one claiming the most difficult steps have already been taken and that it is now simply a case of finishing the job.

The most significant of those steps, in Barcelona's eyes, has been securing the player's desire to join.

Rodri is understood to have already informed City directly that he wants to move to Barcelona, a crucial development that the club insist eliminates the risk of any late change of heart or rival hijack.

Barcelona are not underestimating Man City's negotiating position. (Photo by Annabel Lee-Ellis/Getty Images)

Despite the confidence, Barcelona are under no illusions about the challenge that lies ahead.

Rodri still belongs to City, and the Premier League champions hold the final say on any fee.

Barcelona are aware they cannot underestimate City's negotiating position, particularly given the initial bid never stood a realistic chance of getting the deal done.

The next offer is expected to move considerably closer to City's valuation, and Barcelona accept they will have to make a significant financial effort to turn their current optimism into a concrete agreement.

Still, the belief internally is that Rodri's determination to join will ultimately help bridge the gap.

For now, then, Barcelona wait, hopeful that one of the summer's most ambitious operations can be completed.

title: Fermin Lopez talks Rodri, Ferran, Araujo exit and more – “It’s a shame since he was a captain”

fullText:
Fermin Lopez made his long-awaited pre-season return this summer after overcoming the fractured fifth metatarsal that cost him a place at the World Cup.

The midfielder featured in Barcelona's triangular tournament in Udine, where the Catalans beat Nottingham Forest before losing to hosts Udinese, and afterwards spoke to the media on a range of topics.

Araujo is set to join Liverpool. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images)

One of the main subjects was the departure of Ronald Araujo, who is closing in on a loan move to Liverpool.

Fermin admitted he was sad to see a teammate and captain leave, but wished him well.

"He has come to say goodbye. It's a shame, because he's a captain and I have a good relationship with him. He has decided to continue growing and hopefully he will return next season," said Fermin (h/t Diario SPORT).

The Andalusian was also asked about Ferran Torres and potential new arrival Rodri, though he insisted he did not have much information.

On Ferran's possible exit, Fermin said: "I don't want to go into that, because I don't have the necessary information. He is a good companion and a friend; I hope he decides what's best for him."

Fermin is gearing up for an important season ahead. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

He adopted a similar stance regarding Rodri, who has reportedly chosen Barcelona after his MVP-winning World Cup.

"Rodri is a great player, but he is not at the club. Whatever Deco and the sporting management decide will be fine and, if it has to happen, it will happen," he added.

Fermin, who won a decisive penalty against Nottingham Forest before being rested against Udinese, admitted he is still building up his sharpness after a difficult summer.

"Good. I still have to get into the rhythm, but I felt good. I wanted to play. It's been a very hard summer, but I'm already well and looking forward to this season," he said.

One would expect Fermin to play a key role for Barcelona next season as they look to replace the productivity of Robert Lewandowski and possibly Ferran Torres.

title: Wales must learn from Bosnia loss in Euros bid - Rush
description: Ian Rush says reaching Euro 2028 is a must for Wales as they bid to put their 2026 World Cup qualifying heartbreak behind them.
fullText:
Ian Rush believes Wales must learn from their painful World Cup play-off semi-final defeat by Bosnia and Herzegovina as they bid to qualify for Euro 2028.

The Red Dragons are winless in four matches so far this year and failed to qualify for the summer global showpiece in the USA, Canada and Mexico following their penalty shootout loss to Sergej Barbarez's side in March.

Their task is set to get tougher over the remainder of 2026 as Wales take on Portugal, Norway and Denmark in Nations League A.

But Wales legend Rush believes Craig Bellamy - who came close to leaving the Football Association of Wales to become Burnley boss earlier this summer - has the talent to deliver success with the national side.

"We have to be looking at qualifying [for Euro 2028], it's as simple as that," said Rush.

"Against Bosnia and Herzegovina, we should have won that. They beat Italy as well.

"The Euros are going to be in this country, so we need Wales to be in there."

The former Liverpool striker added: "I speak to Craig quite a lot.

"He's very, very good, so I'm looking forward to a good season and some good rounds from them because it's going to be difficult, looking at Norway, Denmark and Portugal."

Rush urges Liverpool to give Iraola time to succeed

The summer that changed Welsh football

A number of Welsh players have secured moves during the summer going into the 2026-27 season.

Goalkeeper Karl Darlow left Leeds United to join Manchester United while Harry Wilson, arguably the star performer of the Bellamy era, moved from Fulham to Leeds.

Liverpool youngster Lewis Koumas, who scored his first international goal against Ghana in June, is also expected to secure another loan switch away from Anfield having had spells with Birmingham City and Hull City last season.

"I've seen Lewis quite a lot in pre-season, he looks very, very good," said Rush, who scored 28 times in 73 appearances for his country.

"Harry Wilson, he came on in the second half, he was a major influence for Leeds in beating Liverpool.

"We're looking forward, but we've got to keep it as a team, it's up to them to do that, but I can see us doing alright."

Wales start their Nations League campaign against Portugal in Lisbon on 24 September and face Denmark in Copenhagen three days later.

Bellamy's side then host Norway and Denmark at Cardiff City Stadium in October.

The final two matches of the campaign take place in November with Wales travelling to Norway before hosting Portugal.

title: Politicians, private jets and power - the life of a Fifa president
description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino appears to be trying to return to business as usual after the failed World Cup private investment plan - but it may not be that easy.
fullText:
Gianni Infantino stepped off a plane in Cali and was greeted on the runway by the president of the Colombian Football Federation.

Ramon Jesurun, a close ally of Infantino's, saw it as a chance to show his support, with the two men smiling in a photo opportunity for the federation's Instagram account.

Infantino had not travelled to Colombia for any run-of-the-mill meeting on Friday. He would attend the inauguration of the country's new president Abelardo de la Espriella.

Infantino was accompanied by Alejandro Dominguez, the president of South America's football governing body Conmebol, who praised both his record and the "enormously successful" 2026 World Cup, saying "we stand with Gianni".

This is the life of a Fifa president.

It involves building ties with some of the most powerful people in the world, shown by Infantino's relationship with US President Donald Trump.

Before the biggest scandal to hit his tenure - the aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise plan - Infantino was an incredibly powerful figure who appeared bulletproof.

Now, after an apology and stated desire to withstand the backlash of his plan to sell a stake in the men's World Cup to private equity firms, Infantino appears to be trying to return to business as usual.

Uefa's threat to boycott Fifa tournaments still stands. That will be tested with the Fifa Under-20 World Cup set to kick off in Poland in 29 days.

Perhaps emboldened by the support he has received from outside Europe in recent days, Infantino is not going to stand down easily.

But what exactly is the role of the Fifa president?

A cavalcade of blacked out Mercedes, flanked by police cars, rolled into the Fifa headquarters in Rabat, Morocco, earlier this week.

Infantino had summoned a select few members of the Fifa management board to discuss his plan to sell off 21% of the commercial and ticketing business to a private equity firm.

This is how the Swiss-Italian travels - in between flights on the Qatar Airways Executive jet which has been made available to him. The plane enabled him to take up to three flights a day, watching two games, throughout the 2026 World Cup.

That type of arrival does look presidential - only more like a president of a country than a sports body.

It enables him to travel the globe, visiting Fifa's official offices like Rabat, where he was based over the past week as the Fifa Forward Enterprise controversy developed.

In his role Infantino is expected to visit the 211 member nations, to see the grassroots projects Fifa has funded.

Part of his remit is to unify football, which cannot be achieved from within the Fifa headquarters in Zurich.

It requires international travel to attend confederation meetings, and the global tournaments Fifa organises. Infantino needs to build relationships with officials and politicians.

In April, before the Fifa Congress in Vancouver, local authorities rejected a request for a level-four motorcade, usually reserved for heads of state or the Pope.

New Zealand police said they had declined a similar request during the 2023 Women's World Cup.

Alongside the cavalcade of cars and the private charter flights comes a large salary, too, three times what he first earned when elected in 2016.

Infantino, who was paid about £1.3m 10 years ago, now takes home about £4m - a base salary of £2.2m plus a confirmed variable bonus payment of £1.8m.

His predecessor Sepp Blatter was paid a £2.6m package for his final year as Fifa president.

Infantino gets a 'per diem' too to cover expenses and living costs, worth £20,500 a year on top of his salary.

As the head of the most popular sport in the world, it should be expected that there is a wage to match.

Infantino would argue that by driving record revenues and funding for member associations, he has proven he is worth the salary.

Infantino's alliance with Trump seemed to have elevated his status even further.

Many in world football felt that this began to come at the expense of his responsibilities in football.

In May 2025, Infantino had been on a diplomatic tour of the Middle East with Trump and turned up two hours late for the Fifa Congress in Paraguay.

Uefa accused Infantino of prioritising "private political interests" and staged a walk-out.

There was also the Fifa Peace Prize, awarded to Trump weeks before the US invaded Venezuela to depose president Nicolas Maduro and launched air attacks on Iran.

Despite criticism, the Fifa ethics committee did not respond to complaints about Infantino's political neutrality over the prize.

At the start of the year, Infantino made a surprise appearance at the inaugural meeting of Trump's Board of Peace, set up to oversee the reconstruction of Gaza.

The International Olympic Committee, of which Infantino is an invited member, said its rules on political neutrality had not been breached.

However, many felt he had positioned himself too close to the US president.

This was heightened when USA striker Folarin Balogun escaped a ban after being sent off at the World Cup.

It was an unprecedented move by Fifa's disciplinary committee, with Trump saying he had personally called Infantino asking for the red card to be reviewed.

Infantino insisted it was a decision taken by an independent body over which no-one could have an influence.

On the final weekend of the World Cup, Trump and Infantino appeared together at Trump Tower in New York. The US president said he had called the Fifa president who "made another great decision".

Then, perhaps the culmination of Infantino's close association with Trump, came Fifa Forward Enterprise.

The private investor was to be a company linked to the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Uefa says boycott may still go ahead as FA withdraws Infantino support

Uefa boycott right thing for future of game - Bronze

If Infantino goes, who might replace him as Fifa president?

Independent questions of Infantino's methods and decisions are rare because he does not often speak to the media.

In the past four years he has given just two news conferences, both lasting an hour and held before the start of the World Cup.

Other than that, Infantino generally appears in Fifa-produced interviews issued through their official channels.

Before the 2026 World Cup, Infantino tried to head off at the pass any queries about high ticket prices and supporters' visas.

But, at the news conference before the World Cup, his reply of "just, you know, chill, relax" about Somali referee Omar Artan, who had been denied entry to the USA at Miami Airport, sparked concern.

The Fifa statement issued on Wednesday offered some contrition. But there was a rebuke, too.

It gave Infantino the chance to bite back, saying Fifa would "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process".

The allure of the role is great, underscored by the fact there have been just four permanent Fifa presidents since Stanley Rous was elected in 1961.

fullText:
Gianni Infantino stepped off a plane in Cali and was greeted on the runway by the president of the Colombian Football Federation.

Ramon Jesurun, a close ally of Infantino's, saw it as a chance to show his support, with the two men smiling in a photo opportunity for the federation's Instagram account.

Infantino had not travelled to Colombia for any run-of-the-mill meeting on Friday. He would attend the inauguration of the country's new president Abelardo de la Espriella.

Infantino was accompanied by Alejandro Dominguez, the president of South America's football governing body Conmebol.

This is the life of a Fifa president.

It involves building ties with some of the most powerful people in the world, shown by Infantino's relationship with US President Donald Trump.

Before the biggest scandal to hit his tenure - the aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise plan - Infantino was an incredibly powerful figure who appeared bulletproof.

Now, after an apology and stated desire to withstand the backlash of his plan to sell a stake in the men's World Cup to private equity firms, Infantino appears to be trying to return to business as usual.

Uefa's threat to boycott Fifa tournaments still stands. That will be tested with the Fifa Under-20 World Cup set to kick off in Poland in 29 days.

Perhaps emboldened by the support he has received from outside Europe in recent days, Infantino is not going to stand down easily.

But what exactly is the role of the Fifa president?

A cavalcade of blacked out Mercedes, flanked by police cars, rolled into the Fifa headquarters in Rabat, Morocco, earlier this week.

Infantino had summoned a select few members of the Fifa management board to discuss his plan to sell off 21% of the commercial and ticketing business to a private equity firm.

This is how the Swiss-Italian travels - in between flights on the Qatar Airways Executive jet which has been made available to him. The plane enabled him to take up to three flights a day, watching two games, throughout the 2026 World Cup.

That type of arrival does look presidential - only more like a president of a country than a sports body.

It enables him to travel the globe, visiting Fifa's official offices like Rabat, where he was based over the past week as the Fifa Forward Enterprise controversy developed.

In his role Infantino is expected to visit the 211 member nations, to see the grassroots projects Fifa has funded.

Part of his remit is to unify football, which cannot be achieved from within the Fifa headquarters in Zurich.

It requires international travel to attend confederation meetings, and the global tournaments Fifa organises. Infantino needs to build relationships with officials and politicians.

In April, before the Fifa Congress in Vancouver, local authorities rejected a request for a level-four motorcade, usually reserved for heads of state or the Pope.

New Zealand police said they had declined a similar request during the 2023 Women's World Cup.

Alongside the cavalcade of cars and the private charter flights comes a large salary, too, three times what he first earned when elected in 2016.

Infantino, who was paid about £1.3m 10 years ago, now takes home about £4m - a base salary of £2.2m plus a confirmed variable bonus payment of £1.8m.

His predecessor Sepp Blatter was paid a £2.6m package for his final year as Fifa president.

Infantino gets a 'per diem' too to cover expenses and living costs, worth £20,500 a year on top of his salary.

As the head of the most popular sport in the world, it should be expected that there is a wage to match.

Infantino would argue that by driving record revenues and funding for member associations, he has proven he is worth the salary.

Infantino's alliance with Trump seemed to have elevated his status even further.

Many in world football felt that this began to come at the expense of his responsibilities in football.

Uefa accused Infantino of prioritising "private political interests" and staged a walk-out.

title: Norway call on Infantino to resign but two countries back Fifa president
description: The Norwegian Football Federation calls for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to resign after he attempted to sell off stakes in the World Cup.
fullText:
Norway have called on Fifa president Gianni Infantino to resign following his aborted attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, but Mexico and Argentina have voiced their support for the 56-year-old.

Norway have gone a step further than the football associations of England, Wales, Croatia and Albania, all of whom have withdrawn support for Infantino without explicitly calling for him to resign.

"He [Infantino] does not have the institutional trust required to govern Fifa stably in the times we are in," Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) president Lise Klaveness said on Friday.

"There is no going back for Gianni Infantino. The international football cooperation is very much in trouble, and we must have a reason to get together now, and we want to ask the Fifa president to resign now.

"We will see which other countries eventually join in, if that becomes the strategy from the Uefa board. We are not going to ask for an extraordinary [Uefa board] meeting, we will ask him to resign in our dialogue with Fifa."

Klaveness, who is a qualified lawyer, went through a list of concerns that the Norwegian FA has expressed to Fifa during her four-year tenure.

Among them were questions around the awarding of tournaments, the inaugural Fifa peace prize that was awarded to US President ​Donald Trump in December, and the overturning of a ban for American forward Folarin Balogun during the recent World Cup following a phone call from Trump.

Fifa has been approached for comment.

Meanwhile, earlier on Friday the Mexican Football Federation broke ranks with its regional governing body Concacaf to come out in support of Infantino.

Concacaf, which runs football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, called for a "comprehensive reckoning" of Infantino's presidency after he aborted plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

However, 2026 World Cup co-hosts Mexico have backed Infantino's leadership amid widespread calls for him to resign.

"The FMF [Mexican FA] supports president Infantino's leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening," a statement read.

It echoed a statement from Conmebol - South America's governing body - in saying it would reject any attempt to remove Infantino without a vote involving all 211 Fifa members.

Uefa says boycott may still go ahead as FA withdraws Infantino support

Uefa boycott right thing for future of game - Bronze

If Infantino goes, who might replace him as Fifa president?

However, Conmebol did "express its concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken without resorting to dialogue or the institutional mechanisms provided for dealing with this type of situation".

Meanwhile, the football association of 2026 World Cup runners-up Argentina praised Infantino for recognising and apologising for his "errors".

It described his decade-long tenure as Fifa president as "centred on the development of soccer worldwide and institutional strength based on a clear, stable, and transparent governance model".

Infantino is unanimously backed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF), but faces opposition from European football's governing Uefa and Concacaf.

European teams could still boycott the World Cup as Uefa said its conditions had not been met, despite Infantino's plan being aborted.

Uefa has already said it has lost confidence in Infantino, calling the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal a "shabby, back room, opaque deal".

The English FA has sent a letter withdrawing its support for Infantino, while Wales, Albania and Croatia are among other individual associations to have turned their back on the 56-year-old.

Concacaf described Infantino's proposal as "a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first", and that "this recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour".

However, unlike Uefa, it did not go as far as to say it had lost confidence in the Fifa president.

Before Infantino withdrew his proposal, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said it stood "in solidarity" with Uefa and Concacaf in opposition to the plans.

Ordinarily, Infantino would not be able to stand for re-election in March.

The maximum tenure under Fifa statutes is three four-year terms, and Infantino is hoping to be voted in for a fourth time.

However, after replacing Sepp Blatter in 2016, his first term lasted only three years. He successfully argued this one should not count, which allows him to stand again.

Infantino was re-elected in 2019 and 2023 unopposed, and before the FFE controversy it looked certain the same would apply in 2027.

Now Uefa and Infantino's other opponents must try to find a candidate to stand against him.

The deadline for names to be put forward, together with at least five letters of support from member associations, is 18 November.

The election, by secret ballot, will then take place at the 77th Fifa Congress in Rabat, Morocco on 18 March.

If two candidates stand for election, a simple majority of the 211 member associations is required to win.

If there are three or more candidates, 75% of votes is required to win outright. If that threshold is not met, the candidate with the fewest votes is removed and another vote is held.

Once the field is reduced to two candidates, it becomes a simple majority.

Unless Uefa can find a way to unseat Infantino, he has seven months to cement his supporter base.

One way Infantino has always done this is by jetting off around the world and meeting people.

When he was elected in 2016, Infantino declared that Uefa gave him a budget of €500,000 (£430,000), external "to fund flights - mainly flights - around the world" to lobby member associations for votes.

Following Wednesday's meeting of the Fifa management board in Rabat, Infantino jetted off to South America for the inauguration of new Colombian president Abelardo de la Espriella.

Another key tool will be the funding of the 211 member associations, which has enabled Infantino to build loyalty around the world.

This is especially true among developing nations who cannot afford to pay for football development.

Crucially, the latest iteration of Infantino's investment programme, Fifa Forward 3.0, ends in December. It has given all national associations up to $8m (£5.94m) in the latest four-year cycle, a 30% increase on the last one.

When announced, Fifa Forward 4.0 may well up the level of funding again.

For this reason, outside of Europe, Infantino still has a great deal of support and would be the favourite to win an election.

Infantino's staunchest critics, though a few could break the block vote against him.

The African confederation has reaffirmed its unanimous support for Infantino.

While the Asian confederation joined Uefa in criticising FFE it did not issue any statement after the plan was aborted. So far, only Jordan - who did not support Infantino anyway - has said it will not vote for him.

Has strongly criticised Infantino, but Mexico has already broken away to back the president. With so many small nations in the region which benefit from Infantino's funding, it is unknown how much of the rest of the block will hold.

The OFC will not offer a statement until it holds a meeting next month, but earlier this year president Lambert Maltock called Infantino a "leader par excellence" and lauded his investment in grassroots.

A statement issued on Thursday amounted to "do it again and we won't vote for you", but Infantino can still count on Conmebol. Argentina and Paraguay are among the countries to publicly back his re-election.

title: England forward Toney charged with assault
description: Ivan Toney, who was part of England's World Cup squad this summer, is charged with assault following an incident last December.
fullText:
England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault at a nightclub in central London.

The 30-year-old, who plays for Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, was charged on 31 July following an incident on Wardour Street in Soho on 6 December.

The former Brentford striker, who started England's 6-4 win over France in the "bronze final" of the World Cup last month, has been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm and is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on 24 September.

A spokesperson for Toney said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."

After starting his career at Northampton Town, the striker had permanent spells at Newcastle, Peterborough and Brentford before moving to Saudi Arabia in 2024.

He was a surprise selection for England's World Cup squad but apart from the France game, his only other appearance was as a late substitute in the 2-1 semi-final defeat to Argentina.

title: World Cup-winning midfielder has personally informed Real Madrid of decision to join Barcelona
description: In just over 24 hours, Real Madrid have completely slipped out of control of the Rodri operation that they had marked as a summer priority.They were in pole position to land the midfielder and were in...
fullText:
In just over 24 hours, Real Madrid have completely slipped out of control of the Rodri operation that they had marked as a summer priority.

They were in pole position to land the midfielder and were in talks directly with Manchester City. The two parties were seemingly negotiating an agreement but Barcelona used the opportunity to swoop in.

All of a sudden, the Catalans have now leapfrogged Real Madrid in the race and reports have it that the player's transfer to Barcelona is now very advanced. The player has reportedly chosen Catalonia over Madrid.

As relayed in a recent update, Rodri's agent directly told El Larguero via Diario AS the reality of the situation, and where Real Madrid and Barcelona stood all along in the dynamic.

Real Madrid made a massive effort for Rodri. (Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

The agent conveyed that the Manchester City star was 'genuinely grateful' for the respect and interest Real Madrid showed in him over the past two weeks of negotiations.

He also said that everyone at the club, from the president to the staff and even the CEO, did everything possible to sign Rodri and that Real Madrid left no stone unturned. In fact, he confirmed that Los Blancos even submitted an 'unrejectable' offer.

Out of respect for Real Madrid, the player and his agent personally called the club administration last night to thank them for everything and inform them of the player's decision to sign for another club. They wish to avoid any unnecessary drama.

While Real Madrid's project offered a more prominent role to Rodri, it is completely understandable why he chose Barcelona over Los Blancos once the interest arrived.

The Barcelona-dominant Spain NT dressing room played a part in Rodri's decision. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

For starters, his style of football would be more suited to the Catalans' possession-dominant style, and the influence of Pep Guardiola will make the transition easier.

Further, the Barcelona dressing room is dominated by Spanish internationals, all of whom are close to Rodri and played a part in convincing him to join the Catalans.

Jose Mourinho is said to be furious at the development as he prioritised a new defensive midfielder this summer and saw Rodri as the perfect signing. It remains to be seen if Los Blancos push for any new midfielder after Rodri's snub.

This apparently includes Miami Heat legend and former NBA star Udonis Haslem, who has decided to pour in some of his hard-earned money into a newly promoted English Premier League club.

"Basketball has been my life, but I've always respected the culture and impact of football. Proud to announce that last September, I became a minority owner of Ipswich Town Football Club.

He added, "Then I met the people behind the club, and it became clear it was more than just words. It's who they are. That's the only kind of culture I want to be around.

"I'm excited to support what's being built at Ipswich…both on and off the pitch. Miami to Portman Road. NBA to the Premier League. Let's go, Blues!"

Haslem spent his entire career following the ever-so-famous Heat culture, and it feels like the NBA legend has found a club that perfectly embodies that sentiment.

title: South Africa coach Erasmus wary of struggling Argentina
description: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus insists the world champions face a "massive challenge" against Argentina on Saturday despite the recent poor form of their opponents. "Argentina are a quality outfit and we are preparing for a physical and gruelling battle," said Erasmus, a key coaching figure in the 2019 and 2023 Rugby World Cup triumphs of South Africa.
fullText:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus insists the world champions face a "massive challenge" against Argentina on Saturday despite the recent poor form of their opponents.

The Springboks stretched a winning Test run to 11 matches with home victories over England, Scotland and Wales during July in the inaugural Nations Championship.

Facing the same northen hemisphere teams in South America, the Pumas beat Wales, but lost to Scotland, and England in an ill-tempered clash.

Argentina thought they had scored a late try against England, giving them a chance to draw the Test.

When Australian referee Angus Gardner disallowed it after a lengthy review, Pumas fly-half Tomas Albornoz was furious.

The playmaker had to be physically restrained by a teammate and coaches as he remonstrated with the match official and has since been banned for four matches, starting with the Springboks.

However, the absence of the outstanding playmaker and goal-kicker has not soothed the nerves of Erasmus ahead of the one-off Test at the Estadio Jose Amalfitani in the Argentine capital.

"Argentina are a quality outfit and we are preparing for a physical and gruelling battle," said Erasmus, a key coaching figure in the 2019 and 2023 Rugby World Cup triumphs of South Africa.

"They are a well coached team who have tested us in the last few years, so it will be a good challenge for us.

"They gave us one of the biggest hidings we have suffered since I became involved with the Springboks in 2018."

Erasmus said he was unhappy that the international had been called a warm-up match for South Africa ahead of a four-Test home series against New Zealand from August 22.

"This match was not planned with that reason in mind -- it was always about honouring our relationship with Argentina," he insisted.

Because of the All Blacks tour, the annual Rugby Championship southern hemisphere tournament, which includes two matches between the Springboks and Pumas, has been scrapped this year.

South Africa are fielding an experimental team, containing just five probable starters for the first New Zealand Test.

The match marks the return following injuries of fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, locks Eben Etzebeth and Lood de Jager and captain and flanker Siya Kolisi.

Only two of the team that started a 43-0 romp against Wales in Durban -- full-back Aphelele Fassi and scrum-half Cobus Reinach -- keep their places.

Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi has handed a starting debut to tighthead prop Francisco Moreno.

Hooker Leonel Oviedo and back-row pair Juan Penoucos and Juan Martin Scelzo could earn their first Test caps from the bench.

title: Argentina mark World Cup win over England with National Football Teams Day
description: The Argentine Football Association announces 15 July as National Football Teams Day to mark Argentina's 2026 World Cup semi-final victory over England.
fullText:
The Argentine Football Association, external has announced 15 July will be 'National Football Teams Day' to mark Argentina's 2026 World Cup semi-final victory over England on that date.

Bidding for their first World Cup final since 1966, England took the lead in a tense affair in Atlanta through a 55th-minute Anthony Gordon finish.

But with Thomas Tuchel's side sitting deep, Argentina struck in the 85th and 92nd minutes to break English hearts and claim a 2-1 win.

The victory came 40 years after Argentina's previous big World Cup win over England in the controversial quarter-final victory at the 1986 tournament.

After Argentina's latest win the political tensions surrounding the fixture were fuelled as some of their players celebrated while holding a banner reading "Las Malvinas son Argentinas", which translates as "The Falklands are Argentine".

The Falklands, a British Overseas Territory in the south-west Atlantic Ocean, remain the subject of a sovereignty dispute between the UK and Argentina.

Argentina, ruled at the time by a military junta led by General Leopoldo Galtieri, invaded the islands, situated 300 miles off Argentina's east coast, in 1982.

The conflict, which lasted for 74 days between April and June 1982, led to the deaths of 655 Argentine and 255 British servicemen. Three people from the islands also died.

In a 2013 referendum, 99.8% of Falkland Islanders voted to remain a UK territory.

Argentina went on to lose 1-0 to Spain in the 2026 final, while England beat France 6-4 to claim third place.

title: 'Show me they want me' - will World Cup hero Torres stay at Barcelona?
description: Ferran Torres has come under fire from Barcelona supporters after leaving the door open to a potential move away from the club.
fullText:
Ferran Torres will return to Barcelona later this month having cemented his name in the country's football folklore following his extra-time winner to seal Spain's second World Cup triumph.

His profile and marketability has significantly grown and those around him will be keen to ensure he makes the most of a career-defining moment.

But a summer dominated by World Cup celebrations has given way to transfer speculation, fuelled by the forward's own comments during a media tour in the United States.

The 26-year-old is under contract with Barcelona until June 2027 meaning, if he does not reach an agreement with the Catalan giants, Torres will be able to negotiate with another club as a free agent from January.

So, as Barcelona's players gradually report back for pre-season, does Spain's World Cup hero's future remain at the Nou Camp?

The uncertainty surrounding Torres' future has intensified following a series of high-profile television appearances in the United States for a promotional tour with his sportswear sponsor.

Asked where he expected to be playing next season, Torres replied: "I have a contract with Barcelona but, in football, you never know.

"We are waiting to make the right decision. Right now, all I know is that I have to be in training for Barcelona on 12 August. Let's see what happens."

Asked what Barcelona need to do to keep him, he said: "Show me they want me, come to negotiate."

Reflecting on his winner against Argentina in the World Cup final, he added: "I've watched it thousands of times. When I finished the game, I didn't remember the goal. It was unbelievable. I can't describe it with words."

The speculation only increased when he was asked directly about reported interest from Paris St-Germain.

"Every time these teams want you it's a good thing," Torres said. "You never know because in football everything can change in one minute, so I have to be ready for everything."

Asked how he would approach such a career-defining decision, Torres replied: "Trying to think what is going to make me happiest."

Torres' comments have frustrated many Barcelona supporters, who believe he has been too open about the possibility of leaving the club and attempting to strengthen his negotiating position.

Fans have also taken issue with what they see as his carefully chosen wording when discussing interest from other teams, particularly given that he has never established himself as a regular starter or consistently lived up to expectations since joining Barcelona from Manchester City in 2022.

Barcelona remain relaxed about Torres' situation despite the growing uncertainty surrounding his future. They say they will speak to him when he returns to training, as planned.

He was not a regular starter under Hansi Flick last season and ended the campaign with 21 goals and three assists in 49 appearances.

But he is one of the club's most trusted and versatile attacking options, rotating primarily with Robert Lewandowski - who has since signed for Chicago Fire - as a central striker while also providing cover across the front three.

Barcelona are ultimately keen to extend his contract but any new agreement is expected to keep Torres within the existing wage structure rather than include a substantial salary increase.

Reports suggest the club would look to delay formal negotiations until September - after the transfer window has closed - so as not to affect Financial Fair Play calculations and their ability to do business during the current window.

Renewing Torres' deal would also reportedly trigger, external a payment of almost £7m to former club Manchester City, because of a clause included in his contract when he signed in the 2022 January transfer window.

Barcelona have received no formal offers for the Spain international although, as with any member of the squad, they would consider an offer if one were made.

PSG, managed by former Barcelona coach Luis Enrique, remain interested in the forward and are monitoring developments closely as Barcelona prepare to present their proposal.

The forward may feel he heads into those negotiations from a position of strength.

They come with the club still seeking a long-term number nine solution, with a move for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez remaining uncertain.

That means, following Lewandowski's departure at the end of his contract in June, Torres is the only senior Barcelona forward with significant experience of playing as a central striker.

title: Soccer-FIFA apologises to members as Infantino holds crisis meeting amid stake sale fallout
description: FIFA said on Wednesday it had apologised to its member associations for mistakes made over its abandoned proposal to sell commercial rights linked to the World Cup, as
fullText:
Aug 5 (Reuters) - FIFA said on Wednesday it had apologised to its member associations for mistakes made over its abandoned proposal to sell commercial rights linked to the World Cup, as the governing body's leadership reaffirmed its support for president Gianni Infantino after a crisis meeting in Morocco.

Following the meeting in Rabat, attended by Infantino, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom and members of FIFA's management board, FIFA said its leadership had reaffirmed its full ‌support for the president while acknowledging that the handling of the withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal should have been different.

In a statement, FIFA said a separate letter had been sent to FIFA Council members and the 211 member associations apologising ‌for the errors and promising a review.

It added that, with the proposal withdrawn, FIFA would "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process" and would take all necessary measures to protect its reputation.

Vehicles believed to be carrying Infantino and Grafstrom were seen leaving FIFA's Africa office in Sale after the meeting, which ​came amid mounting criticism of Infantino's leadership ahead of next year's presidential election.

The meeting followed last week's withdrawal of a proposal to sell a 20% stake in a new commercial rights entity to private investors in a deal that would have raised about $4.2 billion for football development.

The proposal, which also drew scrutiny because of the involvement of a company with family links to U.S. President Donald Trump, prompted fierce criticism from European soccer's governing body UEFA and other stakeholders, who accused FIFA of poor governance and a lack of consultation.

The apology underscored FIFA's acknowledgement that mistakes had been made in the handling of his proposal for a new commercial rights body, which has become the most serious challenge to his leadership since he became FIFA president in 2016 after triggering a torrent of criticism from UEFA, several member associations and senior FIFA officials over governance ‌and consultation.

His backdown last Friday has done little to assuage those critics, most notably UEFA, ⁠which accused him of selling the soul of the game and has said it no longer has confidence in his leadership.

That has cast a shadow over Infantino's re-election for a fourth term at the FIFA Congress in Morocco in March, which had looked like a foregone conclusion two months ago.

A handful of European federations have withdrawn their backing for the Swiss Italian, but perhaps more damaging are the messages coming from ⁠Infantino's FIFA colleagues.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also questioned Infantino's leadership on Wednesday, saying he has lost confidence in the FIFA president after learning senior advisers had not been consulted on the abandoned proposal.

"I don't have confidence in Mr. Infantino," Carney told reporters, adding that failing to inform senior executives and fellow board members of such a significant proposal "should be fatal" for any leader.

Grafstrom had sent an internal memo to staff lamenting the "sad and reproachable series of events" that led to the project being "permanently abandoned", two sources told Reuters.

"Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission ​and ​its responsibility towards world football continue," the Swede added in the letter, which made no mention of Infantino by name.

His words echoed those of FIFA's Chief ​Operating Officer Kevin Lamour, who said last week that staff had been "deceived" over the plan which he ‌described as the project of one person.

Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned in protest at the plan last week. Arsene Wenger, FIFA's chief of Global Football Development, said he had not been involved in drafting the proposal, and called the decision to withdraw it "absolutely necessary".

Former Portugal great Luis Figo, who had planned to run for the FIFA presidency in 2015, said Infantino should resign over the affair, while UEFA Vice-President Laura McAllister told Reuters the controversy surrounding the abandoned proposal had brought the FIFA president's leadership to a crisis point.

Infantino has spent the past week in Morocco, which will co-host the World Cup in 2030 and whose football association has announced its continued support for him.

The meeting was widely seen as an effort to reinforce support for Infantino and ensure that he emerges from the crisis with enough backing to remain the favourite for re-election in March.

An Extraordinary Congress could be called if 43 or more FIFA member associations make a formal written request for one.

Qatar, which hosted the 2022 World Cup, Kuwait, Lebanon, Sri Lanka, Indonesia and the Philippines have declared ‌their loyalty to Infantino.

Infantino has always enjoyed a lot of support away from the traditional heartlands of the game, where impoverished football associations rely on ​FIFA's largesse to operate.

But European Leagues, which represents more than 1,300 clubs across Europe, said FIFA must not be allowed to "continue taking unilaterally disruptive decisions" that affect ​clubs, players and fans. It also criticised the "impractically short assessment timeline" of four weeks given by FIFA to study the plan ​to expand the World Cup from 48 to 64 teams for the 2030 edition.

AFRICAN ADMINISTRATORS BACK INFANTINO

Leading African football administrators have sent messages of support as Infantino looks to the continent's 54 members for backing. The ‌African confederation (CAF) has yet to take a stance.

The executive committee of the smallest and least wealthy ​regional confederation, Oceania, will meet next Wednesday to discuss their approach.

Under FIFA ​rules, the vote of San Marino, whose men's team are ranked 211th and last in the world rankings, counts as much as that of World Cup winners like Brazil, Germany, Argentina and Spain.

One clear advantage for Infantino as he looks to extend his presidency until 2031 is that no clear candidate to stand against him in March's election has yet emerged.

Jordan FA President Prince Ali bin Hussein has twice stood for the post, and he made his position clear on Tuesday when he ​accused FIFA of "blackmail", saying it had offered to help solve problems in exchange for endorsing Infantino.

"We ‌did not endorse him before and certainly will not now," Prince Ali wrote on social media.

A FIFA spokesperson rejected reports that Infantino had made promises over the host of the 2030 World Cup final.

"It is false and misleading to ​claim the FIFA president has made any promise in relation to hosting the FIFA World Cup 2030 Final. A decision will be made by FIFA in due course," the spokesperson said.

title: Players who turned World Cup heroics into big transfers
description: BBC Sport looks back at some of the players whose standout performances at the World Cup earned a big transfer.
fullText:
The World Cup is football's biggest stage, filled with goals, drama and unforgettable moments - but it can also prove to be the ultimate shop window.

World Cup heroics have transformed players' lives in the past, and Vozinha's recent move to Chilean side Colo-Colo after an impressive tournament with Cape Verde is the latest reminder that the competition still has the power to change careers.

At the age of 40, the goalkeeper's journey from the Portuguese second division to Chile's biggest club may be unique, but he is not the first to get a big move after starring on the global stage.

Here are some of the players whose standout performances at the World Cup earned them a big move.

Similar to Vozinha, Marc-Vivien Foe was an unknown name before the 1994 World Cup.

Despite Cameroon's disappointing World Cup campaign in the USA, compared to their historic run in 1990, Foe emerged as one of the team's best performers during his debut tournament.

A standout game against Brazil caught attention, which then led to a free transfer from Cameroon's Canon Yaounde to French side Lens.

Foe spent four years at Lens and helped them achieve their first league title in the 1997-98 season.

He also played for West Ham United, Manchester City and Lyon, where he won the French League Cup and Lyon's first Ligue 1 title in 2002.

Foe tragically passed away in June 2003 after he collapsed during a Confederations Cup semi-final against Colombia.

Gilberto Silva's first appearance at a World Cup came in 2002, when the tournament was hosted in South Korea and Japan.

The 25-year-old, who played in Brazil's top division for Atletico Miniero, returned home as a World Cup winner who played every minute of every game for Luiz Felipe Scolari's team.

Silva was only brought into the starting XI because Brazil captain Emerson was ruled out by injury.

But, after playing a key role in Brazil's triumph, the midfielder earned a move to Premier League champions Arsenal.

Nicknamed 'The Invisible Wall', the defensive midfielder joined the Gunners from Atletico Mineiro for about £4.5m.

During his six years in north London, Silva won two FA Cups and played a key role in the famous 2003-04 Invincibles side that went unbeaten to claim the Premier League title.

At the age of 22, Javier Mascherano announced himself on the global stage at the 2006 World Cup, where he helped Argentina reach the quarter-finals.

His performances for both his club back in Brazil and at the World Cup drew the attention of European clubs.

Mascherano initially expressed his desire to remain at Corinthians and help the club in their relegation battle.

However, he soon made the move to West Ham United in the summer of 2006 alongside his Argentina team-mate Carlos Tevez, who also impressed at the World Cup in Germany.

Mascherano had a brief spell with the Hammers until the beginning of 2007, leaving to join Liverpool where he featured in their 2007 Champions League final defeat by AC Milan.

Mascherano then played for Barcelona from 2010, winning the Champions League twice and being part of squads that won La Liga on five occasions.

At the age of just 21, Mesut Ozil emerged as one of the world's most exciting young players after he helped Germany finish third at the 2010 World Cup.

After registering four goals and four assists in seven games, Ozil was able to show off his quality and prove he was a standout performer.

Big clubs took note, and by August 2010, Ozil switched Werder Bremen for Real Madrid, for a fee of about 15m euros (£12.4m).

Copa del Rey, La Liga and Spanish Super Cup titles were to follow during his three year stay in Madrid, before becoming Arsenal's record signing for £42.4m in 2013.

James Rodriguez became one of the stars of the 2014 World Cup, scoring six goals for Colombia and winning the Golden Boot after a memorable run to the quarter-finals.

His excellent performances, including his famous volley against Uruguay, earned him a spot in Fifa's team of the tournament.

The volley against Uruguay was later voted as the best goal in the tournament by more than four million people on Fifa's website and won the Fifa Puskas Award for the best goal of the year.

Real Madrid decided to sign Rodriguez from Monaco for about 75m euros (£71m) after the tournament - a move that led to him winning multiple trophies with Los Blancos, including two Champions Leagues.

Well, you knew this one was coming.

Vozinha became a cult hero when Cape Verde claimed their first World Cup point against Spain in the group stage and his social media fame has exploded from 50,000 Instagram followers to nearly 30 million.

After helping his team reach the knockout stages, taking finalists Argentina to extra time in the last 32, Vozinha was named in Fifa's team of the tournament and even had a newly discovered species of sea slug named after him.

Vozinha's career has taken him to Slovakia, Angola, Moldova, Cyprus and, until recently, Portuguese second division side Chaves, but he has always believed himself to be a "big club player".

Joining Colo Colo, the most successful team in the Primera Division (34 titles) and Copa Chile (14), is his career "highlight".

title: Wenger statement puts distance between himself and Infantino
description: Arsene Wenger has come under fire for standing by and allowing FIFA to “sell” the World Cup, which has forced the Arsenal icon to distance himself from the proposal.Wenger has been working at FIFA...
fullText:
Arsene Wenger has come under fire for standing by and allowing FIFA to "sell" the World Cup, which has forced the Arsenal icon to distance himself from the proposal.

Wenger has been working at FIFA since leaving his role as Arsenal manager in 2018 and appears to play an important role within the organisation. This meant many believed proposals of that nature would have passed through him and that he should have stopped them before they reached the public domain.

However, that did not happen and FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under serious pressure to resign following the controversial proposal. Other FIFA officials who did not step down and were perceived to have allowed or supported the proposal have also faced significant criticism in recent days.

Wenger has been among those criticised, but he has now explained his role within the organisation to make it clear that he was never involved in the proposal when it was drafted.

He said, as reported by Give Me Sport:

"The recent events at FIFA deserve some clarity from my side.

"At FIFA, I am the Chief of Global Football Development.

"Together with my team, I oversee the data analysis of the game, the FIFA online training centre, the development of youth education through 60 academies across 60 countries where they are most needed, and youth competitions around the world.

"In addition, I am a technical adviser to IFAB.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger's statement was intended to clarify his responsibilities within FIFA and distance himself from the proposal. He stressed that his work focuses on football development rather than strategic planning, while reaffirming his belief in an independent FIFA that operates with commitment, transparency, and integrity.
